score.headline: Blocking conditions must be resolved before approval.

recommendations.action: Reduce impervious cover by 18 percentage points (permeable paving, green roof, or open landscape)
Substitute 35% of each material with its lower-carbon alternative
Redesign the footprint to retain the 9 heritage-class trees on site, recovering 230 m2 of canopy
recommendations.composite_tradeoff: green 94.5 -> 92.7 (improves by 1.8), but carbon intensity rises 39.5 -> 42.9 because the same materials are spread over a smaller footprint. Composite impact moves +0.3.
recommendations.note: Canopy preserved rather than replaced. Saplings do not substitute for retained mature canopy on any useful timescale.

relocation.method_note: Composite = 0.35*spacing + 0.25*connectivity + 0.25*flood + 0.15*access. Each criterion is reported separately so it can be challenged on its own. Flood uses distance to NATURAL watercourses (nallas, rivers) as exposure; engineered stormwater proximity is deliberately not a siting bonus.
relocation.data_limit: Only PMC-mapped parks and gardens are considered. Private gardens, institutional grounds and undeveloped municipal plots are not in this dataset, so viable_count understates the true options.
